problem.claim: Feature upsampling across arbitrary vision features and resolutions without encoder-specific training.

gap.claim: Existing learning-based upsamplers require retraining for each feature extractor and therefore do not generalize to different feature types at inference time.

contributions.claim: AnyUp is an inference-time, feature-agnostic upsampling architecture applicable across feature types and resolutions without encoder-specific training.
The authors report that AnyUp supports varied feature types, preserves feature semantics, and applies efficiently across downstream tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: An inference-time feature-agnostic architecture for universal feature upsampling.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that AnyUp achieves a new state of the art for upsampled features.
The authors report generalization across different feature types while preserving feature semantics.
The authors report that the method is efficient and easy to apply to a wide range of downstream tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work targets feature upsampling across arbitrary vision features and resolutions without encoder-specific training.
Prior learning-based upsamplers are described as requiring retraining for each feature extractor, limiting inference-time generalization across feature types.
AnyUp is proposed as an inference-time, feature-agnostic architecture intended to address this limitation and improve upsampling quality.
The authors report state-of-the-art upsampled-feature performance, cross-feature generalization, semantic preservation, and practical efficiency.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a concrete deployment constraint—retraining for each extractor—with an architecture explicitly designed for inference-time feature agnosticism.

lessons.interpretation: A strong method framing can connect a specific limitation directly to a matching design property.
lessons.application: When presenting a general-purpose method, state the recurring adaptation burden precisely, then name the design property that removes or reduces it.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the method is intentionally specialized to one encoder, task, or feature family.

unknowns: The abstract provides no metrics, datasets, baselines, or experimental conditions supporting the state-of-the-art, generalization, semantic-preservation, or efficiency claims.
The downstream tasks, supported resolutions and feature types, and meaning of “preserves feature semantics” are unspecified.
